transcript: Well, you know, it took a long time to get this vote. I worked for five years to get this vote. Harry Reid opposed it, and I met with him on several occasions. And in fact, you know, Harry Reid used to be four-odden. We reminded him of that by putting out about two million viewers on our Facebook showing video clips of him debating Byron Dorgan over auditing Fed back in the 90s. We never had much success. We finally got the vote this time. We did get 53 votes in favor. So that is a significant milestone in the sense that we got a majority of people to vote for audit the Fed and we got to vote. The other side argues that, oh, they already are audited. Well, it's kind of like saying, yeah, they're audited to know how much money they spend on coffee, donuts, and salaries. But they really aren't audited on the main part of what they do and where their money is located. So for example, uh... few years ago brankey came before the uh... congressional committee now engrais and ask him you know where did uh... you know the trillions of dollars go that you uh... used during the crisis in 2008 and the auditor had, you know, Bernanke had no answer. The auditors have no answer because the auditors aren't allowed to look at the transaction concerning their assets. Now, we did have a one-time special audit that was stuck in Dodd-Frank, and this was something that my dad pushed for. And through that, we learned that there was $16 trillion worth of loans that occurred during the crisis. Some of this, in fact, maybe as much as a half a trillion went to foreign banks. and foreign institutions. And there's a lot of questions that go on every year through the Federal Reserve that we have no idea. They say that we know all of the assets and they'll show you a big book that has all the assets, but they don't individualize it so you don't know what mortgages are held. You don't know whether they're valued appropriately. And it really is just not much of a look into the Federal Reserve decision-making as far as interest rates go. And so we think the current audit that they say they have is a farce and we're going to keep pushing the issue.
